blocking.section: Runbooks > Region loss (non-home, steps 4 and 5); Figure 2
blocking.issue: Step 4 says a lost Cluster stops its Environment's promotion. Control plane and GitOps, a dependency, says the opposite. Plan members are only connected Nodes, and an empty plan completes at once. So a Rollout to the lost Region's Cluster completes with no delivery, and its promoted digest advances. In step 5 the returning Nodes then activate that Revision with no canary. An operator following step 4 expects a stalled promotion and does nothing. There is nothing to pause, because the Rollout is already `complete`. Figure 2 repeats the error. It also runs `ruralz rollout status` against CT before the alt branch, which is impossible when Region B was the home Region.
blocking.evidence: HA doc, step 4: "Promotions run Clusters one at a time, so a lost Cluster stops its Environment's promotion: pause affected Rollouts with `ruralz rollout pause`, or let them roll back, and retry after recovery." Step 5: "On return, Nodes redial and receive their assigned Revision". Figure 2: "Op->>CT: ruralz rollout status per Cluster, pause promotions that need Region B". Control plane and GitOps, Rollout plan table: "Members | Connected Nodes that ACKed any Revision, or all connected Nodes if none has; others are late." and "Late or zero Nodes | Late Nodes join the final batch and never lag; an empty plan completes at once".
blocking.fix: Rewrite step 4: "A Rollout to a Cluster with no connected Nodes has an empty plan and completes at once. Its promoted digest advances, and its Nodes would activate that Revision on return without a canary. While a Region is lost, hold promotions into every Environment that has a Cluster there. Under `requireApproval`, approve nothing. Otherwise, freeze merges to the tracked branch, or first commit `requireApproval: true` to `control/environments.yaml`, which tightens a gate and so applies without approval." In step 5, before geo weight is raised, add: "Run `ruralz rollout status <cluster>` for each Cluster in the Region. Revert any Rollout that completed with an empty plan during the loss, or confirm that its Revision already passed a canary elsewhere." In Figure 2, change the message to "hold promotions into Environments with a Cluster in Region B", and move it and the heartbeat line into an `else` branch so they are not shown for the home-Region case. Add an Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops: should a plan with zero members, or with far fewer members than the last published Node count, stay `pending` instead of completing?

blocking.section: Runbooks > Region loss (home Region, step 5); Runbooks > Ruralz Control rebuild from Git (steps 4 and 5); Game days GD-10
blocking.issue: Step 5 cannot be carried out as written. It tells approvers to "approve only up to the commit each Cluster's Nodes serve". But only one queued promotion record exists per Environment, and a newer commit replaces an older unapproved record. `ruralz rollout approve --env` can approve only that queued record. So when the branch head is newer than the commit the Nodes serve, an approver can only approve the head or reject it. Environments without `requireApproval` take the head automatically. Either way, reconnecting Nodes activate a Revision that no canary tested. After a restore, rejecting the record also fails: the restored assignments are up to one backup interval old, and the new `storeEpoch` resets sequences, so a Node that moved on after the backup is silently rolled back when it reconnects. The runbook claims the opposite ("their reconnect delivers nothing"). Rebuild step 5 and the GD-10 pass criterion rely on the same impossible step.
blocking.evidence: HA doc, home Region step 5: "Under `requireApproval`, approve only up to the commit each Cluster's Nodes serve (rebuild step 4); then their reconnect delivers nothing." Rebuild step 5: "Let promotions complete in `promotion.from` order before Nodes connect, as in home Region step 5". GD-10: "No Node changes its active digest". Control plane and GitOps: "the target Environment queues a promotion record (source, Environment, digest), which replaces an older unapproved one." CLI and API surface: "`ruralz rollout approve --env prod` shows the queued record's source, digest and diff impact ... so a record a newer commit replaced is never approved." Fencing: "a new epoch resets sequences".
blocking.fix: Replace step 5 with a procedure that can be carried out. (1) Before Ruralz Control ingests Git, find each Cluster's served commit. Use `ruralz bundle diff <bundle-dir> <admin URL> --env <env>` against sample Nodes' `/config/dump` at the candidate commits; after a restore, also compare with the digests in the restored assignments. (2) In Ruralz Control's process configuration (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-1), point the Git source at a recovery ref that holds that commit, not at the tracked branch. Let the empty plans complete to it, and approve under `requireApproval`. (3) Only after Nodes reconnect and report matching active digests, point the source back at the tracked branch, so newer commits roll out with a canary. If Clusters of one Environment serve different commits, say that the runbook cannot align them without a delivery, and route that case to OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-3. State that a restored assignment older than a Node's active digest re-delivers the older Revision unless step (2) runs first. Change GD-10 to pass only when every Cluster's promoted digest equals its Nodes' active digest before reconnect. Change GD-9 so it checks the same condition.

blocking.section: Runbooks > Ruralz Control rebuild from Git (steps 1, 5 and 6)
blocking.issue: An operator cannot complete the rebuild from this runbook. First, step 5 needs approvals under `requireApproval`, but a rebuild loses all users and bindings. Step 1 creates only an `admin` and a `security-admin`, and no role includes `approver`. Approvers also need mandatory TOTP. A commit without a verified signature from a key registered to a Ruralz Console user needs two distinct approvers, and no signature keys exist after a rebuild. No step creates these accounts. Second, step 6 re-enrolls serving Nodes with tokens from `ruralz node token`. But a Node ignores the token while `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/identity/` holds a valid identity. The runbook never says how a serving Node discards its identity (a Drain and restart per zone, as in OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-4 option (b)). So the claim that "traffic never changes" is unsupported.
blocking.evidence: HA doc, step 1: "create the first `admin` and `security-admin` (OQ-deployment-topologies-11). Enrollment records are lost either way, so every Node re-enrolls in step 6." Step 6: "Re-enroll Nodes Cluster by Cluster with tokens from `ruralz node token` ... so traffic never changes." Control plane and GitOps: "no role includes `approver`"; "A commit without a verified signature needs two distinct approvers"; TOTP is "mandatory for `admin`, `security-admin` and `approver`"; the Enrollment token "is ignored once `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/identity/` holds a valid identity".
blocking.fix: Add a step between steps 3 and 5. An `admin` creates at least two `approver` accounts with TOTP, bound per Environment, and registers commit-signing keys, or plans for two approvers per unsigned commit. Rewrite step 6 as a concrete per-zone procedure: Drain the zone's Nodes with `ruralz node drain`; move `identity/` aside and keep `lkg/`; restart each Node with a token from `ruralz node token --cluster <name>`; then check with `ruralz node list` that each Node's active digest equals the promoted digest before starting the next zone. Say that this procedure is the current answer and remains blocked on OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-4. Replace "traffic never changes" with "traffic changes only by the capacity of the zone that is draining (target)".

blocking.section: Degraded modes > Local rate-limit fallback; Failure catalog (FC-4, FC-9, FC-11); Runbooks > Region loss (steps 2 and 3); Game days GD-4

A search finds no definition of any of these symbols in the document.

Link it to the Consistency and accuracy bounds section.

blocking.section: Backups > Taking and checking backups (rule 4); Game days
blocking.issue: The document gives two different cadences for the restore drill, and one of them cannot be met. An operator building a drill calendar from this document cannot tell which to follow. Rule 4 also says to prove "every" backup restorable monthly. With hourly backups, which the document requires, that means about 720 restores a month, and each restore needs an offline trust-root signature.
blocking.evidence: Backups rule 4: "Prove every backup restorable monthly with GD-9 (target); an unrestored backup is unverified." Game days: "Each runs quarterly (target) and gates the milestone shown." Backups > What to protect: "Hourly (target)". Control plane and GitOps: a restore needs "a root-signed anchor set with a new online key".
blocking.fix: Change rule 4 to: "Restore the newest backup into an isolated scratch deployment monthly (target) with GD-9, and verify the signature and decryption of every backup automatically at creation." Change the Game days sentence to: "Each runs quarterly (target), except GD-9, which runs monthly (target)." In GD-9, add that the scratch deployment uses a name that production Nodes cannot resolve, and state how the drill anchor set is signed (offline root, or a drill-only root) so that monthly drills do not use up offline-key ceremonies.
